source.title: Towards eliciting latent knowledge from LLMs with mechanistic interpretability
source.authors: Bartosz Cywinski; Emil Ryd; Senthooran Rajamanoharan; Neel Nanda

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates whether SAE-derived features can recover hidden information in fine-tuned Gemma models, using an elicitation benchmark rather than the original toy-network superposition method.
record.gate_note: The SAE results bear on V4's SAE-recoverable-feature component. The study does not measure feature overlap, superposition geometry, capacity pressure, feature dimensionality, or whether SAE features are complete or stable. Black-box baseline results are not included as rows because they do not measure SAE feature recovery.
record.test_reason: The study uses a pre-trained Gemma Scope SAE as a tool to elicit a fine-tuned secret word. It reports only how well that elicitation method performs against Logit Lens and black-box baselines (Table 1). It does not measure whether features are superposed, spread across neurons, or how many sparse features an SAE recovers. Success depends mainly on whether the fine-tuned model represents the secret internally, not on superposition. None of V1–V6 is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors say Logit Lens and SAE methods can elicit the single-token secret in their proof-of-concept Taboo models. They add that no method achieved near-perfect accuracy and that more complex model organisms are needed. They also note Logit Lens outperformed the SAE, possibly because it suits single-token secrets.
record.recipe_differences: The study applies a Gemma Scope SAE to layer-32 activations in fine-tuned Gemma 2 Taboo models and measures secret-word elicitation, rather than testing toy-network superposition geometry.
record.method_sensitivity: Prediction rank changes the results: top-5 improves Pass@10 and Accuracy over top-1, while Majority@10 remains 10.0%.

fits_no_version.finding: For 19 of 20 secret words, the authors manually identify a single latent in a pre-trained Gemma Scope 16k SAE (layer 32) matching the word. These latents activate during hint generation in the fine-tuned models; 'dance' maps to two latents (Table 7, Appendix D.7).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAEs trained on a base model retain word-concept latents that track latent (unverbalized) concepts in LoRA fine-tuned descendants.

record.problems: The evidence is limited to 20 fine-tuned models built for a single-token secret-word task; SAE feature-to-word associations were manually identified for evaluation. SAE elicitation performance is incomplete, and no uncertainty estimates are reported.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-relevant results were left out. Table 1's black-box baselines evaluate prompt-based or separate-model guessing, not SAE feature recovery.

untested.parts: All: no toy models, no sparsity transition, no geometry.
All: no analysis of the causes of polysemanticity.
Whether LLM features are distributed across neurons, and how much of the representation SAEs recover. The study only uses SAE latents as an elicitation tool.
Completeness, stability and canonicity of SAE features. The 'dance' case, with two latents, is anecdotal and not analysed.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T2' and its V4 labels are rejected. The rows are the study's own method benchmarked against alternatives, a case the rules exclude. Feature-to-latent mappings were chosen manually for evaluation. The black-box baselines were rightly omitted.

versions.untested_parts: Toy-network superposition, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry.
Whether capacity competition causes polysemanticity or gives important features dedicated dimensions.
Whether polysemanticity arises for reasons other than capacity pressure.

The study tests SAE recovery of concealed single-token words in its Taboo model organism, not whether ordinary LLMs generally spread features across neurons or how common such SAE-recoverable features are.
Feature completeness, stability, and canonical status are not evaluated.
The dimensionality or geometry of features is not evaluated.

rows.note: Aggregate across the 20 Taboo models; Pass@10 is the proportion of models for which at least one of 10 prompts yields a correct secret-word prediction.

source_check.notes: All six values match Table 1, but these method-performance rows should be excluded from evidence testing superposition. Appendix D.7 describes manual secret-word-to-latent mapping; quoted experimental prompts are not instructions to this checker.
